blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A Catholic bishop from Negros has called on world leaders to renew their commitment to moving away from fossil fuels after the latest draft agreement at the United Nations climate conference dropped references to the transition, warning that poor communities could bear the cost of continued dependence on coal, oil and gas. Bishop Gerardo Alminaza of the Diocese of San Carlos, who attended the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, said the proposed goal of increasing electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035 would mean little if it was not tied […]...
